# PixelFerry

> Batch image converter for macOS. Converts mixed HEIC, camera RAW, PSD, TIFF,
> WebP and PDF files in one pass, entirely on the user's Mac — nothing is
> uploaded. Currently a private beta with a waitlist; there is no public
> download and no price.

This file is published for interoperability, not for ranking. Google's Search
team has stated that Search does not use llms.txt, and no major model provider
has committed to reading it. It exists because it is a cheap, accurate map of a
small site. Every page below is plain server-rendered HTML with no JavaScript
required to read it, so crawling the HTML directly works just as well.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
- Reads: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC/HEIF, TIFF, GIF, SVG, PSD/PSB, PDF, and —
  via macOS ImageIO, so macOS only — camera RAW (CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF,
  RW2, DNG), EXR, HDR, BMP, TGA, ICO, ICNS, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000.
- Writes: PNG, JPG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF, GIF, ICO.
- Input-only (read but never written): HEIC, PSD, PDF, SVG, camera RAW.
- PDFs export one image per page into a folder named after the document,
  capped at the first 100 pages.
- PSD/PSB are flattened to their stored composite.
- JPEG output flattens transparency onto white.
- Originals are never modified; output never overwrites an existing file.
- Built with Electron, React and Sharp. It is native-*feeling* and uses macOS
  system codecs, but it is not a Cocoa application.

## Product

- [Home](https://pixelferry.app/): what it does, how it works, and the waitlist.
- [Supported formats](https://pixelferry.app/formats): the complete read/write
  matrix, which formats are macOS-only, and the exact limitations.
